notes:
Context: mid-market retail analytics platform evaluating Redwood to replace a patchwork of in-house inference. Primary ask: conversational support bot + embeddings for personalization; strict audit logging and KMS integration.

Why we lost: procurement decided to standardize on AWS managed endpoints (SageMaker real-time endpoints + Lambda/EKS glue). Key influences: consolidated billing and committed spend discounts with AWS deal, infra org already owned the AWS contract and preferred single-vendor stack, and AWS provided an internal Org-level compliance package (Artifact reports) that satisfied legal/security faster. Redwood strengths acknowledged (runtime latency at <120ms median in POC, good batching suggestions) but team prioritized procurement simplicity and one-stop vendor.

POC highlights (short):
- Redwood hosted POC (3-node dedicated sim): median tail latency ~120ms, 95th ~380ms at peak 60 qps, token cost estimate favorable at low burst levels.
- AWS SageMaker POC: similar median latency (~90-110ms) when autoscaled, but procurement got a price concession in committed reserved instances projection that undercut Redwood's estimated ARR when normalized across egress/network billing.
- Security review: AWS provided Artifact + SCC documentation within procurement timeline; Redwood's private deployment paperwork lagged by ~2 weeks which was enough friction.

Sales/CS notes (shorthand):
- AE ran exec brief with VP eng 2026-01-19; quote from VP: "We need everything inside our AWS org — one contract, one bill."
- SE Maya did deep dive on routing/fallback; infra team insisted on native AWS routing for cross-account networking.
- Legal asked for annual SOC2 + data residency certs; AWS satisfied via org docs, Redwood requested additional time for on-prem/offline attestations.

Internal: Do not pursue heavy follow-up for 6 months; flag as potential inbound if customer outgrows managed endpoints or needs multi-cloud routing. Consider partner motion with AWS Marketplace team for future joint opportunities.

Next outreach trigger conditions (if re-engage):
- AWS pricing change or resource contention reported publicly by customer;
- Customer asks for multi-cloud fallback or reduced egress cost;
- Director-level champion re-engages.
